item.text:
**3B.8 Research Note**

Bottom line: **mostly negative**. I found repeated evidence that Erdoğan’s government chilled dissent, policed opposition gatherings aggressively, and selectively restricted assembly. The only meaningful pro-side evidence is that **progovernment rallies were allowed and protected**, which shows selective permission rather than broad tolerance.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Weak positive, selective | [Turkey: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says progovernment rallies were allowed and protected by police, so assembly was not banned across the board. But that permission was selective rather than neutral. | 3B.8 |
| Negative | [Turkey: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024 | Authorities routinely banned gatherings by critics, and police frequently used force against peaceful protests, including May Day rallies, pride events, women’s day actions, anti-price protests, and other civic gatherings. | 3B.8; 3B.5; 3B.6 |
| Negative | [Turkish police detain 217 May Day protesters in Istanbul, minister says](https://theprint.in/world/turkish-police-detain-217-may-day-protesters-in-istanbul-minister-says/2065973/) | Reuters | 2024-05-02 | https://theprint.in/world/turkish-police-detain-217-may-day-protesters-in-istanbul-minister-says/2065973/ | Erdoğan said May Day protests would not be allowed at Taksim Square; police cordoned the area, used tear gas and rubber bullets, and detained 217 people. This is direct evidence of retaliation against peaceful assembly. | 3B.8; 3B.5 |
| Negative | [World Report 2024: Türkiye](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey | HRW says provincial authorities repeatedly banned protests critical of the government, often ignoring domestic court rulings, and police violently detained demonstrators linked to leftist and Kurdish groups. | 3B.8; 3B.5; 3B.1 |
| Negative | [Digital News Report 2024: Turkey](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey | The report describes continued tight media control and notes legal changes that increased risk for journalists, activists, and ordinary citizens to talk politics online. That supports a broader chilling environment around dissent and organization. | 3B.8; 3B.6; 3B.3 |
| Negative | [Türkiye government removes elected opposition mayors](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/07/turkiye-government-removes-elected-opposition-mayors) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-11-06 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/07/turkiye-government-removes-elected-opposition-mayors | HRW says the government removed elected mayors, detained a mayor on terrorism charges, and police violently dispersed protests. That is selective punishment of opposition organization, not protected dissent. | 3B.8; 3B.5; 3B.1 |

**Search gap**

I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence that Erdoğan broadly allowed peaceful protest, dissent, or community organizing **without** retaliation or chilling restrictions. The evidence instead shows a selective system: progovernment assembly tolerated, critical assembly constrained, and opposition activity often punished.
